topIssues.title: flaky test: `TestInteropFaultProofs_InvalidBlock`
topIssues.author: maurelian
topIssues.body:
https://app.circleci.com/pipelines/gh/ethereum-optimism/optimism/139419/workflows/feb351e1-7e49-410d-a1ee-27a572f0e50e/jobs/5877424

Job `memory-all-opn-op-reth-fusaka`, merge-queue run for ethereum-optimism/optimism#23771 (contracts-only change), 2026-11-10.

```
Error Trace: op-devstack/dsl/eoa.go:392
             op-acceptance-tests/tests/superfaultproofs/superfaultproofs.go:1196
             op-acceptance-tests/tests/interop/proofs/serial/interop_fault_proofs_test.go:81
Error:       Received unexpected error:
             operation failed permanently after 5 attempts: not found
Messages:    invalid exec msg receipt not found
```

About 10s before the assertion, chain 902 reorged out the unsafe block (13) that carried the invalid exec message tx:

```
WARN L2 reorg: existing unsafe block does not match derived attributes from L1 component=supernode chain_id=902
  err="transaction 0 does not match ..." unsafe=ce53f5..f22801:13 pending_safe=ac50d9..a4c010:12
```

The mismatch is in the L1 info deposit (different L1 origin), so the tx is dropped and its receipt is never found. Looks like a race between sequencing and L1 derivation rather than a code regression. CircleCI insights also shows a failure in `memory-all-kona-op-reth-fusaka` (1/100 runs on develop).

topIssues.title: kona-node: prevent delegated finalized-head regression
topIssues.author: joshklop
topIssues.body:
A stale delegated source can make Kona request a backward finalized-head update. This is the finalized-monotonicity scope of the delegated derivation parity tracker.

## Reproduction

With local unsafe=30, safe=20, finalized=10, a delegate reports an existing finalized block 5. FinalizeTask checks only that the target is no higher than safe, sends an FCU with finalized=5, and records finalized=5 if EL returns VALID.

The actual Kona engine unit test proves the backward request and acceptance logic. It does **not** establish that real op-reth accepts a finalized regression. EL rejection could instead cause recovery errors.

Compare [Kona finalization](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/optimism/blob/49efa52bcb3ecaeea390d333de63b37b8650aa75/rust/kona/crates/node/engine/src/task_queue/tasks/finalize/task.rs#L32-L75) with [op-node's external finalized monotonicity guard](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/optimism/blob/4f0f0eaf92b923f61d11a9405b88880999399529/op-node/rollup/engine/engine_controller.go#L1535-L1538).

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Older finalized references do not emit backward FCUs or regress CL finalized state.
- [ ] Repeated identical finalized references remain harmless while allowing legitimate pending EL synchronization.
- [ ] Conflicting hashes at the current finalized height are rejected safely rather than silently replacing finality.
- [ ] Preserve hash-pinned lookup, height validation, and safe/finalized ordering checks.
- [ ] Cover older, identical, conflicting-same-height, and legitimate advancing targets.
- [ ] Keep the implementation independent of catch-up liveness and forkchoice delivery/retry fixes.

Confirmed on deployed `49efa52` and PR #23627 tip `2763f5e`; relevant code is unchanged on develop `cfec650e57`. Implement as an independent PR against develop.

Parent tracker: https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/protocol-team/issues/545 (target November 5, 2026).

topIssues.title: kona-client: the library cannot be built for a no_std target
topIssues.author: yoshidan
topIssues.body:
`kona-client`'s library side — `fpvm_evm`, `interop`, `single` — never references `kona_std_fpvm`; only the two binary sources, `src/kona.rs` and `src/kona_interop.rs`, do. But `kona-std-fpvm` and `kona-std-fpvm-proc` are declared unconditionally in `[dependencies]`, so cargo builds them for the library too. `kona-std-fpvm` reads the preimage oracle over file descriptors (`std::fs::File`, `std::os::fd`) and carries no `#![no_std]`, so a consumer that wants only the library cannot build for a `no_std` target:

```
error: `std` is required by `kona_std_fpvm` because it does not declare `#![no_std]`
```

No feature avoids it today: `client-tracing`, the only one, enables `kona-std-fpvm/tracing`.

We hit this building an Intel SGX enclave. The OP Stack light client in [datachainlab/optimism-elc](https://github.com/datachainlab/optimism-elc) uses `kona_client::fpvm_evm::FpvmOpEvmFactory`, and the enclave is built for a custom `x86_64-unknown-unknown-sgx` target with `-Z build-std=core,alloc`, where no `std` exists at all.

`kona-client` is also absent from `no_std_packages` in `rust/justfile`, so `just check-no-std` does not cover it.

### Proposal

Move both dependencies behind a new `fpvm` feature, gate the two `[[bin]]` targets on it with `required-features`, and have `client-tracing` enable it. `default` still enables `client-tracing`, so the ordinary build is unchanged; only a consumer that opts out with `default-features = false` sees a difference. Adding `kona-client` to `no_std_packages` would keep it from regressing.

We have this working against `kona-client/v1.9.0` and are glad to open the PR if the approach looks reasonable.

topIssues.title: op-acceptance-tests: run a subset of the super fault-proof tests on PR CI
topIssues.author: nonsense
topIssues.body:
The op-e2e super fault-proof tests (`op-e2e/faultproofs/super_test.go`) are the only tests that build the op-e2e interop SuperSystem and run its interop migration on the live L1. They need cannon, so PR CI skips them: they run only in the `develop-fault-proofs` workflow after merge, or on a branch through a `fault_proofs_dispatch` pipeline. A change that breaks the SuperSystem world or the migration is found only after it lands.

Port a few of these cases to sysgo, so they run on PR CI:

- create a super game
- play one full super game
- one step with a large preimage (the op-e2e version, `TestSuperCannonStepWithLargePreimage`, has been skipped since April 2025)

The `memory-all-*` acceptance jobs already build the cannon prestate and the kona binaries, and `op-acceptance-tests/tests/interop/proofs` already plays super games on worlds that the same EIP-7702 helper (`op-e2e/e2eutils/transactions/setcode.go`) migrates. The other super fault-proof tests can stay post-merge.

Raised in the review of #23668, which moved the SuperSystem world from `interopgen` to op-deployer.

topIssues.title: kona-node: recover when the EL rejects a delegated forkchoice update
topIssues.author: einar-oplabs
topIssues.body:
Part of ethereum-optimism/protocol-team#545.

## Summary

When the execution layer (EL) rejects a delegated forkchoice update with `INVALID_FORKCHOICE_STATE`, kona-node needs a recovery policy. Both op-geth (`SetCanonical` before its finalized checks) and op-reth (`on_canonical_chain_update` before `ensure_consistent_forkchoice_state`) make the requested head canonical before rejecting it. A delegate whose head does not descend from kona-node's finalized block can therefore leave the EL on its fork after a rejected update, and kona-node's reset then walks a chain that misses its own finalized block.

This scope was split out of #24004 (#23910) and #24005 (#23911). Three Fable 5.1 xhigh review rounds showed that each recovery mechanism added there brought new edge cases. Those PRs keep the pre-existing behavior for a rejected forkchoice update, which is to reset the engine.

## Scope

- Classify a rejected delegated forkchoice update. Look up the engine's finalized block by hash to tell "the delegate's chain does not descend from finality" apart from "the EL lost finality". When the EL still holds finality, restore the EL's canonical chain by resending the engine's own forkchoice.
- Do not retry a rejected delegated head on every poll. Do not remember a transient rejection, such as a safe hash the EL has not stored yet.
- Blame the label that actually moved: a cross-safe-only update must not mark the local-safe head as rejected.
- Make the sync-start walk refuse a chain that is not on the finalized block (op-node `ReorgFinalizedErr` parity) without letting a delegate's head stop the node. Restore and retry. Classify only a genuine finality mismatch as retryable, and treat a missing L1 origin that is actually a fork as a fork.
- Add a `synchronize` backstop that keeps safe and local-safe at or above finalized, without making the reset path fatal.
- Correct a stale safe label even when the verified cross-safe head sits below it.

## Open findings carried over (from the round-3 Fable reviews of #24004 and #24005)

- `FinalityNotRestored` wraps permanent sync-start errors, so they are retried forever.
- A restoring forkchoice update rejected because the EL lost finality loops the reset.
- During EL sync, a different block in the EL at the delegated height does not prove divergence.
- A missing L1 origin at or below the finalized block is classed as temporary before the mismatch check runs.
- A transient `INVALID_FORKCHOICE_STATE` caused by a not-yet-stored safe hash is remembered until the next reset.
- `consolidate()` sends delegated updates through plain `synchronize`, so they are not classified.
- Blame is decided by whether an unsafe head was carried, not by which label was unproven.
- Safe-label rejections are not remembered, which costs three EL round-trips per poll.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] A delegate's head cannot stop the node or loop the engine reset.
- [ ] Mocked Engine API tests in kona-engine for each case above, including an EL that has already made the rejected head canonical.
- [ ] Fable 5.1 xhigh review with no outstanding correctness findings.

topPRs.title: Add Lean proof of the super-aggregation coverage checks
topPRs.author: Inphi
topPRs.body:
Adds a Lean proof that `SuperAggregationInputs::validate` only accepts aggregations whose child outputs form one contiguous chain of super roots from the starting root to the root claim, with one range-derived block per chain and one consolidation step at every timestamp in between.

The Rust is extracted with Charon and Aeneas into `rust/kona/sp1/verification`. The main theorem is `KonaSp1.aggregation_sound`. It assumes child-proof soundness and `l2_sequence_number < u64::MAX`; the README lists the full trust base. `#print axioms` shows only Lean's standard axioms and the opaque super-root hash.

The `super_root.rs` change is only to suit the extractor: loops that returned early from nested or post-`?` positions move into private helpers, with the same accepted inputs and error order. A new test covers a chain-ID mismatch in a later timestamp block, the one loop that was rewritten rather than moved.

CI does not build the Lean project yet. `scripts/extract.sh` regenerates the generated files and `lake build` checks the proofs.

topPRs.title: op-deployer!: run live apply and bootstrap on forge by default
topPRs.author: nonsense
topPRs.body:
Stack 2/7, merge in order: #23663 → #23664 → #23665 → #23666 → #23667 → #23668 → #23669. The whole change, with green CI, is #23647.

The Go script host needs EVM hooks that only op-geth has, so it blocks the move to upstream go-ethereum (#20266). op-deployer already had an opt-in forge path for live deployments. This PR makes that path dependable and the default for live `apply` and `bootstrap`. Genesis deployments, the L2 genesis, `prepare` and `continue` still run on the Go script host; later PRs of the stack move them.

**Effect on users**

- Live `apply` and `bootstrap` run on forge. `--use-forge=false` still runs them on the Go script host, until #23308 removes the flag. `--forge-slow-broadcast` is removed: every broadcast sends one transaction at a time.
- As txmgr did, each transaction gets the node's gas estimate just before forge sends it, a tip of at least 1 gwei, and a fee cap of twice the base fee (at least 1 gwei) plus the tip. Unlike txmgr, forge does not bump the fee of, or resubmit, a stuck transaction.
- forge gets the deployer key in a temporary encrypted keystore that only the user can read, never on its command line.
- op-deployer never compiles. It refuses a contracts bundle whose scripts have no `runWithBytes` entrypoint, and it stops forge as soon as forge starts to compile. So a live deployment needs the contracts release of the same op-deployer release: an `https://` or `file://` bundle of an earlier release is refused (`tag://` locators were already rejected). The default, `embedded`, works, and `--use-forge=false` keeps the Go script host until #23308.
- A contracts bundle is a forge project, so op-deployer does not trust its `foundry.toml`: scripts run without FFI, with file access only to the artifacts, and forge inherits only the environment variables that it needs (`verify-contract` keeps the full environment, for its API key). Each forge script loads every artifact of the project, about 1.3 GB, so forge runs take one of `GOMAXPROCS/2` slots per host.
- forge's output goes to stderr. A failed script reports its revert reason.
- The artifacts-locators page no longer lists `tag://` locators, which op-deployer already rejects. The manual Sepolia test script no longer offers the Go script host as its default engine.
- The forge download detects musl, uses `--cache-dir`, and gives a clear error without network access. The Windows release binaries are no longer built.

**Reasons the diff does not show**

- Each broadcast sends one transaction at a time: without `--slow`, forge waited forever when a node dropped one of several transactions that it sent at once.
- forge runs are not `--offline`: offline, forge requires every solc version of the cache installed even when it compiles nothing. A compile watcher enforces "never compile" instead.
- Every forge run uses its own copy of the compile cache and its own broadcast directory, so that concurrent runs (devstack) do not interfere.
- Bundle builds (Docker, melange, `just forge-build`) run one `forge script` to warm the script cache, and fail when a second run would compile: a single script's compile can choose other solc versions than the project build.
- CI jobs that run op-deployer from the checkout now check out the contracts `lib/` submodules: forge reads the sources to check its compile cache.
- sysgo waits for the L1 transaction index before it deploys chains: geth rejects receipt queries until its first indexing pass, and forge gives up after a few quick retries.
- The test `RetryProxy` gives a client error (4xx, not 429) to the client at once: forge calls methods such as `anvil_nodeInfo` that a proxyd endpoint answers with 403, and the retries held each call for about 40 s.
- The `forge` package tests run in CI only after #23643, which removes the package from the CI exclusion list.

**Reviews**

go-code-reviewer on the transitional code of this PR and the next two. Fixed: the BREAKING CHANGE text named `tag://` instead of `https://`/`file://` bundles, and `--use-forge=false` had no test (a live subtest now covers it).

**Known limits, not fixed here**

Live deploys could keep txmgr by simulating on an anvil fork and replaying, as `continue` does (#23306); the #23300 plan chose `forge script --broadcast`. The RPC URL stays on the command line of forge, which has no environment binding for it. A crash during a broadcast can leave the encrypted keystore and its password file in a directory that only the user can read (forge refuses a password pipe). A forge binary in the cache directory is trusted by its version.

Closes #23302.

BREAKING CHANGE: `op-deployer apply` and `op-deployer bootstrap` run on forge by default; `--use-forge=false` runs them on the Go script host until a later release removes it. `--forge-slow-broadcast` is removed. An `https://` or `file://` bundle of an earlier contracts release is refused for live `apply` and `bootstrap`; use `embedded`, or `--use-forge=false` until the Go script host is removed. Go callers replace `ApplyPipelineOpts.UseForge`, `ForgeSlowBroadcast` and `PrivateKey` with `UseScriptHost` (zero value: forge) and `DeployerPrivateKey`; `pipeline.Env`'s `ForgeClient`, `UseForge`, `L1RPCUrl` and `PrivateKey` with `Forge`; and bootstrap's `UseForge` and `ForgeSlowBroadcast` with `UseScriptHost`. `forge.ScriptCaller` returns `(output, error)` without the recompiled flag, and `forge.Client.SlowBroadcast` is removed. The Windows release binaries are no longer built.

topPRs.title: op-chain-ops: add eth-liquidity-pause command
topPRs.author: karlfloersch
topPRs.body:
Stacked on #23348 (`karl/eth-liquidity-pause`). That PR makes `ETHLiquidity` mirror the chain's L1 pause through the permissionless `L1CrossDomainMessenger.syncETHLiquidityPause()`.

## What it's for

`op-chain-ops/cmd/eth-liquidity-pause` is a small CLI for the ETHLiquidity pause. It has three uses:

- **Devnet gate `interop.eth-liquidity-pause`:** `devnet-pause` → `status --expect paused` → `devnet-unpause` → `status --expect unpaused`.
- **Production verification:** `status` is read-only and works on any chain. Production pausing stays with the guardian's existing DeputyPauseModule flow, and this tool never pauses production. Nothing new is needed in superchain-ops.
- **Mirroring an L1 pause (or unpause, or expiry) to L2:** `sync` is permissionless, so any funded key can run it.

## Commands

- **`status --l2 <rpc>... [--l1 <rpc> --l1-messenger <addr>...] [--expect paused|unpaused] [--json]`**
  - For each chain it reads `ETHLiquidity.paused()` and `pausedL1Timestamp()`.
  - It runs an `eth_call` of `SuperchainETHBridge.sendETH` with 1 wei. A state override funds the dummy `--from`, so the sender needs no balance. It reports whether the call reverts and with which error (selector and name).
  - With `--l1`, it also shows `L1CrossDomainMessenger.paused()`, which is the ETHLockbox pause, and prints `OUT OF SYNC` when L1 and L2 differ.
  - `--expect` exits non-zero on any mismatch. For `paused`, every chain needs `paused()` true, `sendETH` reverting with `ETHLiquidity_Paused()` and, if read, L1 paused.
- **`sync --l1 <rpc> --l2 <rpc> --l1-messenger <addr> ... --key <any funded key>`**
  - Checks that each messenger's `SystemConfig.l2ChainId()` matches the `--l2` it is paired with.
  - Prints the L1 and L2 state per chain and skips chains already in sync (`--force` overrides).
  - Calls `syncETHLiquidityPause()`, waits for the L1 receipt, then polls L2 until `paused()` equals the L1 pause at the sync's block, or `--timeout` passes.
- **`devnet-pause` / `devnet-unpause --guardian-key <key>`**
  - Resolves each chain's ETHLockbox identifier through messenger → SystemConfig → portal → lockbox. Chains that share a lockbox are handled once.
  - Checks that the key is the SuperchainConfig guardian.
  - Calls `pause`, `extend` (if an earlier pause expired) or `unpause` on the lockbox identifier, then runs `sync`.
  - `devnet-unpause` warns if a global pause is still active.
  - Refuses OP Mainnet, Ink, Unichain, their Sepolia chains (10, 57073, 130, 11155420, 763373, 1301) and an L1 of Ethereum mainnet. There is no override flag.

Every flag can also come from `--config <toml>` (see `config.example.toml`). Local `*.toml` files in that directory are gitignored because they may hold keys.

## Usage

```bash
# Production / any chain: read-only
go run ./op-chain-ops/cmd/eth-liquidity-pause status \
  --l2 https://mainnet.optimism.io --l2 <ink-rpc> --l2 <unichain-rpc> \
  --l1 <eth-rpc> --l1-messenger <op-l1cdm> --l1-messenger <ink-l1cdm> --l1-messenger <uni-l1cdm>

# Mirror the current L1 pause to L2 (permissionless)
go run ./op-chain-ops/cmd/eth-liquidity-pause sync --config pause.toml --key <funded-l1-key>

# Devnet gate
go run ./op-chain-ops/cmd/eth-liquidity-pause devnet-pause   --config devnet.toml
go run ./op-chain-ops/cmd/eth-liquidity-pause status         --config devnet.toml --expect paused
go run ./op-chain-ops/cmd/eth-liquidity-pause devnet-unpause --config devnet.toml
go run ./op-chain-ops/cmd/eth-liquidity-pause status         --config devnet.toml --expect unpaused
```

## Tests

None of these tests need a network.

- **Calldata:** encoding for `paused()`, `syncETHLiquidityPause()`, `sendETH`, and SuperchainConfig `pause`/`unpause`/`extend`/`pausable`/`paused(address)`.
- **ABI drift:** a test checks every hand-written signature and custom error against the contracts-bedrock ABI snapshots on this stack, so a rename in #23348 fails here.
- **Revert decoding:** custom errors and `Error(string)` reasons.
- **Safety checks:** production refusal, `--l2`/`--l1-messenger` pairing, grouping chains by shared lockbox, the guardian pause/extend/unpause choice, and `--expect` evaluation, including L1 paused while L2 is not synced.
- **Config loading:** TOML values load into each command, including the example config.
- **`status` end to end:** runs against in-process fake L1/L2 JSON-RPC servers. The cases are paused and synced, unpaused, out of sync, a pre-pause ETHLiquidity, a messenger paired with the wrong chain, and JSON output. The fake rejects `sendETH` without the balance override, as geth does.
- **`sync` end to end:** runs on geth simulated backends with mock contracts. The cases are skip when in sync, `--force` send and wait for L2, a reverting call never sent, and an L2 timeout.

```
go test ./op-chain-ops/cmd/eth-liquidity-pause/...   # ok
go vet ./op-chain-ops/cmd/eth-liquidity-pause/...    # clean
./linter/bin/op-golangci-lint run ./op-chain-ops/cmd/eth-liquidity-pause/...   # 0 issues
go mod tidy -diff                                    # clean
```

I also ran `status` read-only against OP Mainnet and OP Sepolia public RPCs. ETHLiquidity is not initialized there yet, and the tool reports `Error("Proxy: implementation not initialized")` for both reads.

**Not run:** `sync` and `devnet-*` against a live devnet with #23348 deployed. The guardian path (`devnet-pause`/`devnet-unpause`) has unit coverage only for its decision logic.
